gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a named reviewer timed a switch on any of these docks: Dan S. Charlton measured the Sabrent Thunderbolt 4 KVM (SB-TB4K) bringing USB devices back within 1-2 s but the monitors only after about 5 s, and found that it charges one laptop at a time, capped at 60 W.
standout_why: I compared against the cited dockgearhq.com 'Best KVM Switches for Dual Monitor Setups', dockgearhq.com 'Best Docking Stations with Built-In KVM Switch', thunderboltlaptop.com 'Best Dual Monitor KVM Switches' and the top-ranked triedtestedreviewed.com page. None of them has a measurement of its own or one from a named reviewer. Their switch times are the maker's '2-3 seconds' or unnamed owner reports: dockgearhq says 'a few seconds ... over 20 seconds for dual 4K recovery' for the Sabrent. All their wattages are ratings. Dockgearhq already says, from the spec, that the Sabrent and TESmart give 60 W to the active host only. So the new part is a named, timed switch and a measured USB-port power limit, not the charging point itself.
decides: This confirms that the Thunderbolt picks lose on charging and switching. The Sabrent SB-TB4K was measured at about 5 s to bring the monitors back, and only the active laptop charges. The TESmart HDC202-X24 was confirmed at about 60 W, and its front USB ports dropped out of spec past 8.5-9 W each. So for 'two laptops, both charging', the AV Access iDock C20 (rated 60 W to each laptop at once) stays the pick, though nobody has timed or measured it independently. The Sabrent is also listed as unavailable on sabrent.com today at $299.99, which weakens it as ChatGPT's #2 pick.

findings.label: Time to switch (USB devices / monitors)
findings.value: USB keyboard, mouse and devices detected within 1-2 s; monitors about 5 s to register
findings.source_title: Sabrent Thunderbolt 4 KVM Dock Teardown and Review (Dan S. Charlton, 2023-07-13)
findings.note: Hands-on test with a Surface Laptop Studio, a Dell Latitude 5420 and an eGPU, plus monitor simulator dongles. The switch button itself responds instantly (LED). No timing tool is named.

findings.label: Laptop charging
findings.value: 60 W maximum, one laptop at a time
findings.source_title: Sabrent Thunderbolt 4 KVM Dock Teardown and Review (Dan S. Charlton, 2023-07-13)
findings.note: Rated 20 V × 3 A. Included power supply is 120 W (24 V × 5 A). Charlton says to keep USB and Thunderbolt downstream draw near 50 W to hold 60 W laptop charging, leaving about 10 W for the dock.
